# Design: `scalar()` must not read a trailing space as a value (#612)

Full artifact at `openspec/changes/issue-612-scalar-trailing-space/design.md` (worktree `/home/gandalf/IA/brain-issue-612`).

## Approach
One line: `^${key}:[ \t]*(.+)$` -> `^${key}:[ \t]*(\S.*)$`, keeping `.trim()`. Everything else in the change is tests or comments. No consumer code edited.

## D-A Boundary table (today -> after)
- `key: v` -> 'v' / 'v'
- `key:v` -> 'v' / 'v'
- `key:` -> null / null
- `key: ` (one space) -> '' / **null**
- `key:\t` -> '' / null
- `key:   \t  ` -> '' / null
- `key: <NBSP>v` -> 'v' (JS trim strips U+00A0) / **null**  <- the D1 divergence; refusal confirmed
- `key: v  ` -> 'v' / 'v' (trim still earns its keep)
- CRLF `key:\r` -> null / null (drift test's CRLF row unaffected)

CORRECTION to proposal D4's framing (conclusion survives): the repair changes TWO input classes, not one — whitespace-only ('' -> null) AND exotic-whitespace-led values ('v' -> null). The second is monotone toward refusal. The load-bearing half holds: NO block becomes admissible that was not. The weaker half ("none stops being admissible") holds only for the whitespace-only class.

## D-B Prefix class
Keep `[ \t]*`. Dropping it breaks every normal `key: value` read (capture cannot start on the space). `\s*` is THE TRAP: `\s` includes `\n`, so under /m on `findings:\n  - id: F-1` it eats the newline and captures `- id: F-1` inline — a worse rebuild of the bug. It also re-admits NBSP through the prefix, contradicting D1.

## D-C Governance-invariance test location
`brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.test.mjs` — with the CONSUMER. The invariant is a property of actor-check's gates; the durable risk is someone editing a gate into a form that distinguishes '' from null (`at ?? ''`, `typeof === 'string'`). A guard in yaml-block's tests never enters that editor's field of view. Scalar-side boundary table goes in a NEW `brain/scripts/review/lib/yaml-block.test.mjs` (none exists today; only the drift file).

## D-D F2 pin
`parse-verdict.test.mjs:331` rewritten in place, same `#452/#478-F2` id, comment updated to record the flip ("WAS a pinned defect… #477 deferred on scope; #612 landed it… assertion INVERTED on purpose; do not delete the id"). New assertions: `findings: ` + entry -> `[{id:'F-1'}]`, and `'malformed' in result === false`, plus the clean-form control.

## D-E Drift guard — DO NOT TOUCH ITS ASSERTIONS
`yaml-block.drift.test.mjs` does NOT pin regex source text (header says so: behavioral equivalence, "deliberately NOT a source scan"). All 8 rows verified: the repair changes none — the `` ```yaml `` trailing-space row is the FENCE (FENCE_RE), not scalar; the tab-key row fails the column-0 anchor either way; CRLF unaffected. It does NOT trip.
Adding a trailing-space row is the RUBBER-STAMP TRAP: the table observes only `protocol` and `head_sha`, and both gates refuse '' and null identically (that IS D4), so such a row is null/null BEFORE and AFTER — passes unchanged, proves nothing, and reads as if the repair were covered there. It also violates the file's stated charter (rows "vary only the surrounding carrier syntax… never the value's own content").
After the repair it should assert EXACTLY what it asserts today. Only edit: one header-comment line pointing at `yaml-block.test.mjs` as home of the value-side contract.

## D-F Mutation axes
1. trailing space vs none — full revert `(\S.*)`->`(.+)` must go red in 4 files (parse-verdict F2, yaml-block boundary, checkpoint-block, epic-map)
2. leading exotic whitespace — `(\S.*)`->`(.*)`; killed ONLY by the NBSP row (otherwise a surviving mutant)
3. prefix crosses lines — `[ \t]*`->`\s*`; killed by F2 pin + findings-with-entries control
4. prefix exists — drop `[ \t]*`; killed by nearly every existing test (sanity axis)
5. trailing trim — remove `.trim()`; needs a NEW `head_sha: <sha>  ` row or it is a live mutant
6. entry-list-follows vs nothing-follows — a fix inside parseEntryList's block branch instead of scalar passes `findings: `+entries but fails `findings: ` alone -> `[]`
7. decision-block: `actor:`/`head_sha:`/`decision:` whitespace-only still refused
8. actor-check: six-key invariance + `sniffDecisionProtocol('protocol: ')` -> null -> silent, never `addressed`
9. epic-graph: `track: ` moves from its own '' group to '?'/UNCLASSIFIED; `blocks: ` -> []
10. checkpoint-block: error text flips "must be a non-negative integer, got ''" -> "missing the required `counted_lines:` key"
11. NEGATIVE axis (invariant): `sequencing:`, `controls:`, `controls_not_applied:` stay `malformed` BEFORE and AFTER — their KEY_RE probe + `raw !== null` shape absorbs both states. Pin it so a future "simplification" that drops the probe is caught.
Axes 2 and 5 are invisible without new rows. Axis 11 proves the repair did not reach where it had no business reaching.

## File changes
yaml-block.mjs (Modify: regex + JSDoc) · yaml-block.test.mjs (Create) · parse-verdict.mjs (comment only, drop the "still not repaired" claim at 127-136) · parse-verdict.test.mjs (F2 rewrite + nothing-follows + axis-11) · actor-check.test.mjs (six-key table) · decision-block.test.mjs · epic-map.test.mjs · checkpoint-block.test.mjs · yaml-block.drift.test.mjs (header comment ONLY, zero assertion changes)

## Collision with PR #695
REBASE, do not merge. #695 changes where a brain-graph/1 block is LOCATED (near extractFencedBlock, lines 51-54); #612 changes how a value is READ (line 57). Orthogonal semantics, adjacent bytes. #612's reviewable surface is one line; a merge commit hides the conflict resolution where a reviewer cannot diff it. Whoever lands second rebases onto main and re-runs parse-verdict.test.mjs, yaml-block.drift.test.mjs, epic-map.test.mjs. FLAG FOR APPLY: `gh pr diff 695` BEFORE the first edit; re-measure the suite before/after; a second failure is stop-and-report, not fix-forward.

Open questions: none blocking.
